newsitem.title: GERMANY: Joblessness could derail Bonn's EMU budget - wiseman.
newsitem.headline: Joblessness could derail Bonn's EMU budget - wiseman.

text.p: Record unemployment could force the German government to make more budget cuts in order to meet the strict fiscal targets for European monetary union, a member of the government's independent economic council said.

January's rise in unemployment to a record 4.66 million could require another 10 billion marks in jobless benefits than Bonn accounted for, Rolf Peffekoven, one of Germany's so-called "five wisemen," said in an interview with the daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung to be published on Saturday.
But this could cause Bonn to miss the Maastricht Treaty's limit of a three percent ratio between budget deficits and gross domestic product, he said.
"If the government wants to keep to its projected value of 2.9 percent, it would still have to achieve considerable savings in the current budget," Peffekoven said.
The independent council's projection of a 3.3 percent ratio was "more realistic," he said.
Peffekoven said additional jobless spending could be so high because Bonn's budget is based on low unemployment and benefit estimates.
Bonn figured on average 1997 unemployment of 3.95 million, although the Federal Labour Office said on thursday it now projected an average of 4.1 million or more.

"Since the budget appropriation for jobless benefits was already low -- it amounted to 4.1 billion marks after 12.5 billion in 1996 -- you can count on considerably more expenses, which could be just around 10 billion marks," he said.
